recipes.label: Thunderous Sound?
recipes.startdescription: As you and your soldiers 'visit' the local farm as usual, you hear drumbeats drifting from the sheepfold, and soon you and your soldiers feel the urge to dance.

recipes.label: “Talk” with the Doves
recipes.startdescription: Birds in pairs, their song like red thread – what will they bring me?

recipes.label: “Talk” with the Doves
recipes.startdescription: The birds guide us to a small hidden cache.

recipes.label: “Talk” with the Doves
recipes.startdescription: The birds bring us a little story.

recipes.label: Feathered Gift
recipes.startdescription: The lake cannot be visited again. I wrap the Golden Fleece around the blade and send it back; the vitality of Heart flies with the blade – may it be light, may it be clear.
recipes.description: Days later, I receive a reply from the birds. A whisper from the lower heavens.

recipes.label: About the Commission
recipes.startdescription: With enough force, let it arc across the sky and fall into the lake's heart with the gift.

recipes.label: About the Commission
recipes.startdescription: As if still running through an old dream, the sound lingers. Does the lake-dweller yearn to recall the days of freedom?

recipes.label: About the Commission
recipes.startdescription: “Vitality” – I chew the word like an unripe fruit. Is it the surging of blood? The beat that will not stop? What is it that is like Heart, and like a drum? The lake can no longer be entered, but the sword-keeper has left me an opening – a throwable object can send the offering into the lake's heart. I look toward the beasts on the hillside.

recipes.label: Exchange Secret Messages
recipes.startdescription: Visitors are rare; the sword-keeper dwelling in the lake does not mind exchanging a few idle words with me.
recipes.description: I have no stories to tell, and she has no secrets to share. First we meet eye to eye, then I sink beneath the lake's surface.

recipes.label: The Named One of the Lake
recipes.startdescription: The lake's surface is still and reflective as a mirror; the moon's reflection in the water is identical to itself. A pale woman rises from the depths of the lake, causing not a single ripple, cradling a jagged iron weapon like a mother holding her child. Her eyes are closed – but her head still turns to examine me. Is it disdain in her expression, or sorrow?
recipes.description: “Human killer,” the woman whispers, but her lips do not move. “My treasure and I have been reunited but a moment, and already you have come to take it. Then take it – this sword has been passed many times from Pearl-hand to Scar-hand, and returned many times as well. But mark my words, human killer – after but another moment, this weapon will return to this lake.” She gives me the sword in her arms.

recipes.label: Are We Both Wounded by Serpents?
recipes.startdescription: She carefully examines my wound, shakes her head, and says, “I cannot heal you,” but she is happy to make a small change to my wound.
recipes.description: “I cannot guarantee that this is not a small continuation of strife.”

recipes.label: Are We Both Troubled by Serpents?
recipes.startdescription: She looks at the maiden with slight confusion, shakes her head, and says, “I envy you, favoured child.” She turns to me, “We cannot leave the lakeshore. Could you fetch something for me?”
recipes.description: “I cannot guarantee that this is a small cessation of the storm.”

recipes.label: Invoke the Red Grail to Replenish Flesh and Blood
Something Burrows Inside Me?
recipes.startdescription: Something is burrowing inside me! This is by no means a good death. Fog covers my eyes – and I never wear glasses – my eyes are being eaten by worms! Melting! Before my world vanishes, Evangelina Polevaya runs toward me; I strive to run the other way, then I am embraced in the darkness. I am drowning. I am burning. [If you still have at least five wounds or five mental traumas when this final time runs out, you will succumb to the worms.]

recipes.label: Reach a Conclusion
recipes.startdescription:
Every pair of connected souls preserves an initial question: “What are we?” And what interests me more is that this question has never been answered.
Her tears are my mirror; she tells me: a sword fell from the sky – perhaps I am that sword, perhaps not. Thus I am enlightened by her all-encompassing eyes; she tries to lead me away from the flood of honours.
We are sword and thief, honour and wound, commander and daughter of serpents.

[You may now try to communicate with the maiden]

recipes.label: Reflect on the Poison Within...
recipes.startdescription:
The venom slowly stagnates in the limbs and blood, embedded in bone and flesh. In drowsy visions, no divine inspiration comes – only repeated self-questioning and curses from one's own soul: What will I die of? When will I die? Where will I die? Who will come for me? Who will go with me? Why must I die?
The final answer is only poison! Poison! Poison!...

[You can treat the snake venom by brewing a special potion; of course, a priestess's blessing can also transform the wound.]

recipes.label: Contemplate the Method of Double Victory...
recipes.startdescription: The victory of my beloved and me...

recipes.label: Contemplate the Method of Double Victory...
Key to the Wrong Door...
recipes.startdescription: The Spider Door – the door that was wrongly opened...
recipes.description: The Spider Door, wrongly opened, is sacred to the Mother of Ants; the Necklace Lords passed through it, and now their daughters still guard it. Sulochana is now in seclusion; our situation is special. With the right introduction, they may still be drawn to us, and Sulochana will open the door for us. The House does not accommodate lovers; this unconventional door is the most suitable for my unconventional beloved. Despite the danger and difficulty, I need the Key of Night to manifest once more.

recipes.label: Preparations of a Hundred Blades...
recipes.startdescription: It is now difficult to verify what weapon – or how many weapons – the Colonel used to slay the Seven-Coiled...
recipes.description: It is now difficult to ascertain what weapons the Colonel used, and how many, to slay Qipan. Yet we must not rely on a single blade alone. We must gather a diversity of sacred, heterogeneous artifacts: the nail, the sword, the claw, the skull, the spear, weapons forged from one's own flesh, and also that which once slew Qipan. Only when all arms are assembled can one face the aberrations in the wilderness.

recipes.label: An Unusual Bond...
recipes.startdescription: I must forge a bond with the maiden that transcends the mundane, rooted in the depths of the soul...
recipes.description: I must forge a bond with the maiden that transcends the mundane, rooted in the depths of the soul. Then I shall learn the secret rites and raise her to the position of Priestess – the Mother of Ants' former office. This will be a path of gnosis. After she inherits the ancient secrets, she will bless me.

recipes.label: One's Own Duty
recipes.startdescription: One does not exist for the other; one cannot replace the other...
recipes.description:
One does not exist for the other; one cannot replace the other.
As for my own duty – the duty of a soldier – I still need to walk the soldier's path. To engage in warfare, to push the battle toward a turning point.

recipes.label: The Wasteland Beyond the World...
recipes.startdescription: Where the world's epidermis is broken – the desolate land that deviates from mortal fate...
recipes.description: Where the world's epidermis is broken – the desolate land that deviates from mortal fate. There still lurks a serpent that is not of serpents. I will slay them and drive them out here. This is the purification of the world's wounds.

recipes.label: Contemplate the Method of Double Victory...
Pilgrimage to the Shrine of the Iron God
recipes.startdescription: If I wish to imitate the Colonel's feat – together with the Priestess – I need to know more details of the story, and more truths.
recipes.description: The shrine is silent. No Named One pays me any heed.

recipes.label: Seven Steps to Slay the Seven-Coiled
recipes.startdescription: The air inside the shrine grows cold. My vision flickers; soon I can see only darkness. Something has come here.
recipes.description: I close my eyes. In the shadows, I hear the uneven footsteps of the Named One, Antigonus the Cyclops, accompanied by the light footsteps of a lady. “Human killer,” he says in a deep and solemn voice. “This is another side of a well-known story.”

recipes.label: Have the Priestess Bless Me
recipes.previewDescription:
If I am to defeat the seven-headed monster, I must receive a priestess's blessing.

[This will consume a vial of Raw Venom]
recipes.startdescription: The Priestess first undoes my clothing and cleans my poisoned wound with clean water. She heats a silver needle red-hot over a lamp wick and slowly opens the skin around my wound, exposing the festering interior to the surface. But the pain I expected never comes. She leans close to me and sucks the poison from my body. Sometimes I really wonder where she learned these techniques.
recipes.description: One key reagent is still missing – I need some snake venom as the raw material.

recipes.label: Have the Priestess Bless Me
recipes.startdescription: She filters the venom through her own clothing, then heats and stirs it over the campfire, while mixing in a small amount of another liquid.
recipes.description: The venom is then applied to the wound's surface; I need to wait two hours. Thus the ritual will protect me from the serpent's magical harm, just as the Priestess once did for the chiliarch.

recipes.label: Have the Priestess Bless Me?
recipes.startdescription: One key reagent is still missing – I need some snake venom as the raw material.

recipes.label: Raise an Assistant
recipes.startdescription: I swear by my scars to the Mother of Ants: may the kingdoms favour my princess as they favour me, may the beasts revere my beloved as they revere me.
recipes.description: Just a little more.

slots.label: Gaze of the Mother of Ants

recipes.label: Raise an Assistant
recipes.startdescription: I swear by my scars to the Mother of Ants: may the kingdoms favour my princess as they favour me, may the beasts revere my beloved as they revere me. I will raise her higher under the Priestess's gaze.
recipes.description: She rises from the blood, reborn from the wound. She has passed through the door to perfection.

recipes.label: Raise an Assistant
recipes.startdescription: I show the Mother of Ants my wounds and my resolve; the little sisters shall call her sister, and she shall rise higher under the Priestess's care.

recipes.label: Already at the Highest Rank
recipes.startdescription: She rises from the blood, reborn from the wound. She has passed through the door to perfection.

recipes.label: Raise an Assistant?
recipes.startdescription: If I can find the right place and the right means, and add enough influence to draw an Hour's attention, she can realise more of her potential.

recipes.label: The Guest Has Arrived
recipes.startdescription: I hurry to greet the guest, bringing the leg bone.

recipes.label: Another Ligeia
recipes.startdescription: “No need to say more,” she says, taking a drag of her cigarette, her eyes smiling. “You have courage and daring. I hope you won't regret your choice. Also, let me see that kin of mine – don't worry, I ate on the way.” I cannot read the look in her eyes, but she will not leave before I call Evangelina Polevaya.

recipes.label: A Dance, an Acknowledgment
recipes.startdescription: “She told me some things about how to become a true woman, and about the Twins. I'm not entirely sure I understand the true mysteries...” After Evangelina Polevaya dances into my arms, I am certain she did not learn anything strange.
recipes.description: Everything is normal.

recipes.label: A Dance, an Acknowledgment
recipes.description: Everything is normal.

recipes.label: The Ligeia's Return Gift
recipes.startdescription: “<sprite name=lantern>?”
recipes.description: <sprite name=grail>...

recipes.label: The Ligeia's Return Gift
recipes.startdescription:
“<sprite name=grail>, <sprite name=heart>, <sprite name=winter>.”

[This will directly give you the stele]

recipes.label: The Ligeia's Return Gift
recipes.startdescription:
“<sprite name=grail>, <sprite name=moth>, <sprite name=knock>.”

[Another Ligeia will come]
recipes.description: After leaving a pile of bones behind, the devourer departs. I crouch with Evangelina Polevaya beside the bones, poking through them with a branch. In the end, we together grasp a leg bone with a distinctive bite mark, one on each end.

recipes.label: The Ligeia's Return Gift
recipes.startdescription:
“<sprite name=grail>, <sprite name=heart>, <sprite name=knock>.”

[This will give you the final key ingredient to cure the snake venom]

recipes.label: One Up, One Down
recipes.startdescription: I will provide all the support I can to ensure this ravenous Ligeia does not devour my cherished one.
recipes.description: I should not have met so hastily.

recipes.label: Talk While Eating...
recipes.startdescription: Currently, the safe distance between them is ten metres, but that distance is not safe for her. I toss the remains to the devourer.

recipes.label: Talk While Eating...
recipes.startdescription: Currently, the safe distance between them is ten metres, but that distance is not safe for her. I toss the corpse to the devourer.

recipes.label: Communicate with the Devourer
recipes.startdescription: I will provide all the support I can to ensure this ravenous Ligeia does not devour me.
recipes.description: I watch her consume my soldiers, leaving nothing behind.

recipes.label: Communicate with the Devourer
recipes.startdescription: I offer the remains to the devourer. She eats the corpse, and then she eats the spokesperson.

recipes.label: Communicate with the Devourer
recipes.startdescription: I offer the corpse to the devourer. She eats the corpse, and then she eats the spokesperson.

recipes.label: Communicate with the Devourer
recipes.startdescription: “<sprite name=mortal>.”

recipes.label: Let the Maiden Communicate with the Devourer?
recipes.startdescription:
I should not ring the bell without preparing a gift.

[Please prepare a 'Gift' before sending the maiden to speak]

recipes.label: Communicate with the Devourer?
recipes.startdescription:
I should not approach a Ligeia so closely, but I can have my subordinates speak on my behalf.

[Unless I can find a 'person' who shares a common language with her, the ally will be devoured after the conversation]

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription: I close my eyes gently, listening with my ears to the most ethereal bell in the church, and thinking with my heart of my most beloved.
recipes.description: My love was not answered.

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription: The church candles are dim. I bow my head in worship. Though I see nothing, I clearly sense Saint Agony standing behind me – her narrow, pale feet silent beneath the coarse nun's robe, clutching keys, blades, candles, and her own head. She softly tells a story: a great serpent in the wilderness once devoured everything. A priestess showed the warrior where to strike. She then says that serpents were never the greatest threat – with sufficient preparation and effort far beyond the ordinary.
recipes.description: As her voice fades, there is no one behind me, only a faint coolness lingering. My heart pounds; I smell flowers and hints of meaning, and every window and door in the church has been quietly opened.

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription:
I leave the command post and go alone to the church – not for the dire situation, nor for immortal slaughter, but for a maiden's heart.

[I may be able to upgrade this intent]
recipes.description: Understanding eludes me.

slots.label: Gaze of the Mother of Ants

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription: Then her elder sister answers me; I hear her descending the steps, the metal keys jingling as she moves. “Listen,” she says softly, “to what she thinks.”

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription:
The Mother of Salvation casts her care upon us; we give thanks and receive the blessing.

[I may be able to use this influence]
recipes.description: @#mem.joy|Winter sunlight, stained-glass refractions – a time of gentle breezes.#mem.calm|Candles flicker, dust settles – a wordless ritual.#mem.grief|The icon lowers its gaze, the pews are cold – I remember that longer silence.#influenceknock|A lock turns in an old wound; a door opens from the ribs; breath flows freely.#influenceknockc|Bricks are removed, keys hidden under tongues; words leak from the cracks.#op.motherofants|The shadow climbs the altar, arms encircle; the scab on the throat is pierced; I can speak again.@

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription: The Mother of Ants coils around the wound, around the church, and around every crack and door.

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription:
The Mother of Ants is skilled in poison and healing; if we are devout enough, the poison in the soldiers can be drawn out.

[I may be able to heal the soldiers]
recipes.description: The prayers end; we leave with the wounded, praying for a miracle.

slots.label: Gaze of the Mother of Ants

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription: After the prayer, the poisoned soldier vomits a thick black fluid. We let him rest in bed for a few days until he fully recovers.

recipes.label: Seek Revelation in the Church
recipes.startdescription:
The Colonel, with the help of the Mother of Ants, slew the Seven-Coiled and became an Hour. To this day, they may still maintain some cooperative relationship. If I pray devoutly to the Many-Armed Mother, she will surely bestow her gospel.

[This will reset this influence]

recipes.label: Cure the Incurable Snake Venom
recipes.startdescription: The Grail can stimulate my flesh, Winter can calm my pain, Knock can open the rotting interior, Nectar can quicken my life. I have met all the necessary requirements – it is time to begin.

recipes.label: Cure the Incurable Snake Venom
recipes.startdescription: The Grail can stimulate my flesh, Winter can calm my pain, Knock can open the rotting interior, Nectar can quicken my life. I have met all the necessary requirements – it is time to begin.

recipes.label: Cure the Incurable Snake Venom?
recipes.startdescription: I need the right formula, the right person, the right tools and location.

recipes.label: Brew Venom
recipes.startdescription: Not enough – ordinary venom cannot heal my wounds. I need more ingredients to brew a potent venom.

recipes.label: Done
recipes.startdescription: I chant the prayer, and the Daughter of Venom answers me.

recipes.label: Done?
recipes.startdescription: I am missing the most important part – a priestess's blessing. With her divine power, my ailment will surely be cured.

recipes.label: Add Alcohol
recipes.startdescription: The Lavilin family has declined, but their wine still circulates in the secret world. Now I have a bottle in my hand – a little sweet, a little sour.

recipes.label: Add Powder
recipes.startdescription: This powder, no matter where it is, carries a smell of the sea. Perhaps it is mixed with salt – I hope it is not counterfeit.

recipes.label: Add Oil
recipes.startdescription: This bottle of oil comes from something that has ended. I had best not dwell on where it truly came from – let the beasts guess.

recipes.label: Brew Venom?
recipes.startdescription: First, I need a vial of venom as the base.

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn?
recipes.startdescription:
I need enough Winter power to fill it.

[Items placed here will be consumed]

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn
recipes.startdescription: I place them together in a black box; when I open it again, there is a crack at the bottle's mouth, but it is done.

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn
recipes.startdescription: I place them together in a black box; when I open it again, there is a crack at the bottle's mouth, but it is done.

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn
recipes.startdescription: First I press my mouth to the bottle's mouth, then my breath, my tears... then it is done.

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn
recipes.startdescription: My brother is not dead, but his blood still carries a chill.

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn
recipes.startdescription: I smash the teeth of this corpse and grind them to powder.

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn
recipes.startdescription: The air is filled with the breath of Winter.

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn
recipes.startdescription: The air is filled with the breath of Winter.

recipes.label: Fill the Oil of Grey Dawn
recipes.startdescription: The air is filled with the breath of Winter.

recipes.label: This Won't Work
recipes.startdescription: I bring it near the bottle's mouth. The solution remains unmoved.

recipes.label: This Won't Work
recipes.startdescription: I bring it near the bottle's mouth. The solution remains unmoved.

recipes.label: This Won't Work
recipes.startdescription: I bring it near the bottle's mouth. The solution remains unmoved.

recipes.label: Serpent Attack
recipes.startdescription: Upon entering this area, my unit encountered a serpent. It was cunning and powerful, devouring many of my soldiers; had my comrade not arrived in time, I would have paid a much heavier price. According to my comrade, the serpents on this battlefield have changed. If I want to fight them, I must put in more effort; but if I only wish to avoid them, I think I have some guidance.

recipes.label: Crush the Pearl
recipes.startdescription: I hope I don't mix up the two pearls.
recipes.description: It's crushed. I hope I didn't make a mistake.

recipes.label: A Second Believer
recipes.startdescription: After our people return from the church, they carve small crosses on their gunstocks.

recipes.label: A Second Believer
recipes.startdescription: After our people return from the church, they offer a brief prayer before taking off.

recipes.label: A Second Believer
recipes.startdescription: After our people return from the church, they paint crude crosses on the gun barrels with white paint.

recipes.label: A Second Believer
recipes.startdescription: After our people return from the church, they pin small crosses between their collars.

recipes.label: Power of Faith
recipes.startdescription: At midnight, the wounded moan incessantly from the pain of their wounds. Then a slender, many-armed woman walks through the barracks, touches the wounded where it hurts, and vanishes into the depths of the room. That night, the soldiers sleep as peacefully as children.

recipes.label: <color=purple>F A T E D   T I M E</color>
recipes.startdescription: Then Stalingrad vanishes. The street beneath my feet becomes ancient Mansus-stone. A cobalt sky glimmers beyond my reach. Before me, Ligeia Medusa inserts her writhing, pallid key into the Stag Door. Its old wounds groan in pain, and the scars on my body groan with it as the door opens fully. I am blind; I bear scars; I am unopposable. There is light beyond.

recipes.label: Another Path...
recipes.startdescription: Just before the light touches me, I hear her echo from the other side – as if swallowed and chewed, as if scratched and torn. It seems she has gone ahead of me this time.

recipes.label: <color=blue>F A T E D   T I M E</color>
recipes.startdescription: Then Stalingrad fades in cobalt light; the street I tread transforms into ancient Mansus-stone. Before me, the Named of the Twins, Ligeia Medusa, inserts her writhing, pallid key into the Stag Door; it groans in pain, old wounds bleeding golden and boiling blood, and I groan with it as the door opens, my scars bleeding with it. I once made a vow with the sister of the oracular priestess; now she will come, or extinguish my eyes, carve scars upon me, render me unopposable, and the radiance even in war shines like an eternal sun –

recipes.label: The Little Tail Left Behind...
recipes.startdescription:
“Soldiers, why do you stand gazing up at the sky? Go on fighting. The light that hangs over the world does not welcome surrender. Struggle to the last breath.”
The crowd disperses, leaving only a small serpent in its place, at the highest, highest, highest point it can climb – before the broken door.

“What he tears down, he cannot rebuild; what he opens, he cannot close.”...

recipes.label: Far from the Battlefield
recipes.startdescription: The peace of this moment is temporary; stillness makes my thoughts fly, so I write in my diary.

recipes.label: Far from the Battlefield
recipes.startdescription: The peace of this moment is temporary; stillness makes my thoughts fly, so I write in my diary.

recipes.startdescription: The peace of this moment is temporary; stillness makes my thoughts fly, so I write in my diary.

recipes.label: Far from the Battlefield
recipes.startdescription: The peace of this moment is temporary; stillness makes my thoughts fly, so I write in my diary.

recipes.label: The Arsonist
recipes.startdescription: Damn the enemy! I will never forgive them!

recipes.label: In the Chapel
recipes.startdescription: A few pews in the church are still empty; soldiers sit scattered. I raise my hand to greet them – then Polevaya takes my hand, anxious and afraid. The wind leaks through the stained glass and falls upon her face.

recipes.label: In the Flames
recipes.startdescription: Smoke pours through the main entrance; stone pillars crash down. With broken limbs, I lift rubble to open a way for the soldiers. Until only Polevaya and I remain – we try to break out through the side door but run into a corridor. Damn – left? Right? Back against a scorched pillar, the flames draw closer. “Do you understand? I am a monster, pitied by no Hour. I was spat upon beneath the church, feared by all – even though I am human in form, even though I was born human. And you – you unshackled me, you feigned a moment of mercy...” Her fingertips trace the soot on my face, and I kiss her.

recipes.label: Burning Body to Block the Fire
In the Night
recipes.startdescription: Eyes closed, the roar of flames like distant machine guns, like thousands shouting – forward? retreat? or hallelujah? Polevaya grips my wrist; when I open my eyes, there is light at the corridor's end – the pale, cottony daylight of a Moscow winter, and a serpent's shadow on the ground. We stumble out of the church; it collapses as I burst through the main door, but we had just been in the side nave... Evangelina stands by the ruins, her eyes reflecting the embers and me.
recipes.description: I get up, brush the dust off my Red Star uniform. Someone calls for me, someone prays. I walk toward them, taking my lover's hand.

recipes.label: Spending Time: Farm
recipes.startdescription:
She finds some abandoned old clothes. She says she wishes tears could become cotton. I express agreement and ask her what I am in her eyes. She is puzzled that I bind tears to her.

“Linen...”

Then she changes it to “Steel needle.”

recipes.label: Spending Time: Provisions
recipes.startdescription: My dry tea tin has become a small can of meat. I know who is responsible. Meat does not refresh, and I cannot find any porridge to mix it with. I learn to swallow like a beast, only afterward remembering I have a knife.

recipes.label: Spending Time: Grief
recipes.startdescription:
She sits with me under a massive rock in the wilderness; her tears still do not stop... I don't understand why she keeps crying.

We talk longer than ever before. In the end, I weep too. Loneliness is no longer loneliness, rest no longer rest.

recipes.label: Spending Time: Joy
recipes.startdescription:
She takes me along the dry riverbeds, showing me the smooth marks on the ground, and the ways of serpents – as if introducing herself... Then a wind suddenly rises – the homeless wind cast out of the sky during the Heaven War.

We stand for a moment; the wind dies, and a flare rises in the distance, radiating light. Every hollow on the ground bursts into colours unseen in ordinary night. She stands still, gazing, unmoving for a long time.

recipes.label: Spending Time: Calm
recipes.startdescription:
She takes me to the empty forest in the early morning; the distance between us is only a bullet's length. The snow of the Caucasus covers the fire in my heart – white forest, white hills, white eyes.

When the cold white sun rises and melts the ice and snow, all becomes my silence – at least part of it.

recipes.label: Gift: The Stone that Holds a Secret
recipes.startdescription: I place this stone in her palm. She weighs the secret in her arms, then runs her teeth across its surface, as if to scrape new patterns from the old object. She closes her eyes and presses the stone to her ear, listening for its pulse. After a long while, she whispers, “Thank you.” I nod. She hides the stone in her clothes. Who in this world does not have a secret they cannot tell? Let alone a maiden on the battlefield.

recipes.label: Spending Time: A Melodious Violin
recipes.startdescription: I open the case, take out the violin, set it to my neck with affected formality, and whistle a tuneless song. She is startled at first, then laughs and demands to learn. I hand her the violin; she imitates my posture, brings her lips close, but only lets out a hissing breath – like a young serpent. Undeterred, she tries again, making a short chirping sound, like a fledgling. Finally, her face flushed, the violin nearly slipping from her shoulder, she returns it to me. I take it, put it back in the case, and close it. The music never truly sounded, but I heard a song of no strings.

recipes.label: Gift: A Suspicious Key
recipes.startdescription: I take out a thin cord and thread it through the key's ring. She lowers her head, eagerly rubbing her neck against my hand – like a keyhole yearning for a key. I order her to sit still. The wound on my hand makes knotting difficult, so I hold the cord's end between my teeth, my lips brushing the back of her neck – a cool touch, like that of an old cellar door-knocker. When we face each other again, I still hold a strand of her hair between my teeth, and an unspoken word.

recipes.label: Spending Time: Cat
recipes.startdescription: A cat saunters to the edge of the camp; neither of us appeals to it. It challenges my authority. I engage in a silent little struggle with the cat. It bristles, hissing at me. The maiden, perhaps to protect me, leans down and hisses back at the cat. The wind passes between us; someone plucks an invisible string. I hiss too. Then coarse laughter erupts from a corner of the camp.

recipes.label: Sweet Fruit...
recipes.startdescription: She exudes fragrance; I smell it. I breathe under her breath; I taste her; I feel a thirst. She strokes my lips. With the divine fire burning in my heart, I long for peace, and tonight peace answers me.

recipes.label: Sweet Fruit...
recipes.startdescription: She exudes fragrance; I smell it. I breathe under her breath; I taste her; I feel a thirst. She strokes my lips. With the divine fire burning in my heart, I long for peace, and tonight peace answers me.

recipes.label: Sweet Fruit...
recipes.startdescription:
Until dawn wakes me, a small toy appears on my left hand.

“Whose is this, my pillow companion?”
“That's you. Doesn't it look like you? Just like the real thing. I thought today would be a good day for a gift.”

recipes.label: Spending Time: Souvenir
recipes.startdescription: When I find her, she is sitting in the camp, stones passing between her fingers again and again. I sit beside her. I am not a talkative person, but today is a good day for heart-to-heart.
recipes.description:
@#mem.joy|I speak of my hopes for the future.
She seems curious and hugs my arm, saying, “I truly hope to see the world you speak of – together. I look forward to it.”#mem.calm|My words are mixed with inner bitterness and confusion.
She smiles, takes my hand, and says, “I don't mind listening more. No matter what happens, I'll always support you.”#mem.grief|I speak of my anger and discontent.
She moves a little farther away, clearly startled. Yet after only half a day, she comes back to me and gives me a hug.@

recipes.label: Spending Time?
recipes.startdescription:
Perhaps now is not a good time to disturb her.

[You can try other topics, or in other locations]

recipes.label: Talk with the Maiden?
recipes.startdescription:
I need to understand her better.

[You must first uncover the maiden's intent]

recipes.label: Beloved
recipes.startdescription: On my barren land, this is my last rose.

recipes.label: Send the Weeping Maiden to Explore the Wilderness
recipes.startdescription: According to her, she knows this place well enough. I believe she can return.

recipes.label: Send the Weeping Maiden to Explore the Wilderness
recipes.startdescription: According to her, she knows this place well enough. I believe she can return.

recipes.label: Send the Weeping Maiden to Explore the Wilderness
recipes.startdescription: She returns before we leave this place, though empty-handed. At least we have not lost anything. But she does not see it that way – she is silent and sad, her tears will not stop...

recipes.label: Send the Weeping Maiden to Explore the Wilderness
recipes.startdescription: She returns before we leave, smiling with both hands behind her back, asking me to guess what she found – beets, sunflowers, potatoes... canteens, thick gloves. I never guess right, and no one knows where they came from.

recipes.label: Emergency?
recipes.startdescription:
At sunset, the maiden runs back to camp in great haste, looking utterly dishevelled – as if frightened by something. I briefly inform my deputy and move out under her direction, and what I see is a weak, dying worm. The Colonel's arts help me drive off this hungry, venomous thing. But I know this is not over; there are definitely more evils from the Mansus nearby. The maiden sobs softly, so I hold her and comfort her as best I can.
Back in camp, I make her a bowl of hot soup. We sit by the campfire all night, and she tells me everything that happened today.
recipes.description: Those things have caught her scent. I must drive them back.

recipes.label: Send the Weeping Maiden to Explore the Wilderness?
recipes.startdescription: According to her, she knows this place well enough. Perhaps she can bring back some useful supplies.

recipes.label: Have the Maiden Extract Venom
recipes.startdescription: I put food in the tent, settle her in, and quickly step away, hoping she can finish soon.
recipes.description: She soon emerges with a small bottle; the liquid inside is enough for our next step. I stroke her and praise her. She is happy to have helped me.

recipes.label: Have the Maiden Extract Venom
recipes.description: She soon emerges with a small bottle; the liquid inside is enough for our next step. I stroke her and praise her. She is happy to have helped me.

recipes.label: Have the Maiden Extract Venom?
recipes.startdescription: We still have some serum in storage, enough for emergencies. This process causes her discomfort – I should not trouble her too often.

recipes.label: Have the Maiden Extract Venom?
recipes.startdescription: My soldiers are suffering – perhaps she can help resolve the trouble caused by other sisters.

recipes.label: Abandon a Maiden
recipes.startdescription: I order her to leave; she follows us for a while, until I order my men to fire at her feet.

recipes.label: Temporarily Leave a Maiden
recipes.startdescription:
Before departure, I make final arrangements. The soldiers' footsteps rustle. When I enter her room, she is sitting on the bed. I crouch beside her, press the toy soldier into her hand, and comfort her that I will soon call her back – this is my duty. She twines a strand of her hair around the inside of my collar. Then she stops crying and nods. I take her hand and lead her to the edge of the wilderness. I watch that white figure disappear into the wasteland, standing for a long while.

[You can only do this once per game]

recipes.label: Call the Maiden Softly
recipes.startdescription: She knows my voice, remembers my scent. If I call her, she will surely answer.
recipes.description: She runs crying into my arms like a lark – this time, tears of joy.

recipes.label: Call the Maiden Softly?
recipes.startdescription:
She knows my voice, my scent. If I call her, she will surely answer.

[I need to go where she can hear me]

recipes.label: Abandon a Maiden?
recipes.startdescription: Having a little sister follow the marching column may bring us many troubles. If I want to abandon this journey, I must sever all ties. If I am only leaving temporarily, I need to give her something I treasure.

recipes.label: Strange Occurrences?
recipes.startdescription: Your soldiers often complain of strange crying in the night. Some of the faithful even prefer to sleep outside.

recipes.label: Occupy the Strange Church to Stabilise Morale?
recipes.startdescription: False gods always fear that people may grasp the truth. I send a few loyal and efficient men to carry out the raid; those inside fall into chaos at once. We accomplish the occupation without effort.
recipes.description: Soon we discover the church's cellar, filled with various torture devices. In the deepest cell, only empty shackles remain.

recipes.label: Pray in the Strange Church?
recipes.startdescription: The more one thinks, the farther one drifts from the divine. I clasp my hands to my chest as usual, but this time no clergy are present, and I cannot quiet my heart.
recipes.description: At last, a young cleric leads me out. As I rise, I hear strange sounds from beneath the floor. The cleric grows visibly nervous and urges me out, almost pushing me away.

recipes.label: Investigate the Church
recipes.startdescription: Who truly are the agents of the gods? Ignoring the local priests' warnings, I lead an assault team into the church to find out.

recipes.label: Victory!
recipes.startdescription: The Colonel is stern, the Mother of Ants cruel. The headless golden sheep has passed, but its fleece still stirs.

recipes.label: Mansus Source Cut Off
recipes.startdescription:
The power of the Mansus pours from the world's wounds like black smoke, burning the fingertips, then flows back into its nest at the moment of sealing. With each crack repaired, the monsters' screeching weakens, their movements grow slower, as if their hidden sinews have been pulled out.
At the same time, in the instant the Mansus-flow is severed, the great serpent at the centre of the battlefield reveals an opening – like a door about to close.

recipes.label: Victory!
recipes.startdescription: Following the source of the sound, we smash through the old wooden floor and descend into the long-sealed dark dungeon. There, imprisoned, hangs a maiden...

recipes.label: Victory!
recipes.startdescription: Following the source of the sound, we smash through the old wooden floor and descend into the long-sealed dark dungeon. There, imprisoned, hangs a maiden.

recipes.label: Escort the Wounded Maiden Home
recipes.startdescription: “Oh, really... thank you, truly, thank you,” she says between sobs. “Those priests were terrible –” she keeps only her left eye open. “It's wonderful that you've taken their place, just as they took my home.” Speaking of home among people far from home is inevitably moving. “Yes, thank you for freeing me. If you... if you would be willing to take me... home. Of course... I know the way.”
recipes.description: “Oh... it wasn't like this before. Perhaps you could come in with me. The path is narrow, only the two of us – safe, I promise.”

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair?
recipes.startdescription: The space here is narrow, only wide enough for two to pass. I need someone who can open the way – preferably one who was once its keeper.

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: I have found the right person – it is time to set out.

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: Before setting out, I need to bring some weapons and tools to deal with possible difficulties.

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: Crawling forward...

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: The depths of the cave are filled with rubble; we need to clear the obstacles to continue.

recipes.label: Pass with Power of Heart
recipes.startdescription: We are strong – we will clear the obstacles.

recipes.label: Pass with Power of Forge
recipes.startdescription: We are practical – we will clear the obstacles.

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: We could not find a way through the rubble, so we withdraw for now.

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: Crawling forward...

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: The door is tightly shut – whether deliberately damaged or worn by time, I cannot tell.

recipes.label: Pass with Power of Knock
recipes.startdescription: We understand opening; we open doors; we are meant to pass.

recipes.label: Pass with Power of Forge
recipes.startdescription: We have the great power of Forge; we break down the door; we are meant to pass.

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: We could not find a way to open the door, so we withdraw for now.

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: Crawling forward...

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: A thick, fetid miasma – reeking of decay and the memory of blood.

recipes.label: Pass with Power of Heart
recipes.startdescription: Heart protects; corruption cannot touch us. The miasma cannot penetrate.

recipes.label: Pass with Power of Grail
recipes.startdescription: Flesh is red; what fear of blood? The miasma cannot penetrate us.

recipes.label: Pass with Power of Winter
recipes.startdescription: Remain silent, hold your breath. The miasma cannot penetrate us.

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: I see the shadow of the serpent devouring humans – this is the dwelling of inhuman things, forbidden to mortals. Retreat!

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: In the darkness, I grip the hand in front of me...

recipes.label: Explore the Remote Lair with the Maiden
recipes.startdescription: In the darkness, I grip the hand in front of me. In a daze, I hear its call and a strong sensation of being enveloped. I am squeezed, scraped – moving back from adulthood and military service, to earlier, and earlier still – to a farmstead, in sulphur-yellow haystacks. I recall a time when I had no abilities and no responsibilities – a child, unnamed, without nationality, without faith. I taste milk again, play with the umbilical cord. Then a pain I have never known – a cleaving force pressing into me, cutting like feathers through the body. I nearly die, until another force bursts from my wounds and joyfully pushes me out of the ignorant darkness –
recipes.description: When I wake again, I am lying intact on the maiden's lap. She is wearing clothes I have not seen before. “Evangelina Polevaya,” she says as she helps me up. I do not answer. I find my cap in the grass nearby. We are on a sunlit hillside. No sunflowers – a red sun is falling. “They imprisoned me with me; now I can never go home – any home.” Her tears fall with the sun.
